project.title: Bitcoin supply theorem (Prove2me) — semantic graph prototype

nodes.title: Issuance cap
nodes.statement: The subsidy schedule's issuedBelow(n) is less than MAX_MONEY for every natural height n.

assumptions.name: n
assumptions.meaning: Arbitrary natural number of blocks or subsidy periods, in the formal statement.

nodes.title: Per-block UTXO supply update
nodes.statement: For a reachable state S, an accepted next block increases UTXO total by at most the core block subsidy.

assumptions.name: hR
assumptions.meaning: State S is reachable under the formal model.

assumptions.name: hv
assumptions.meaning: The block validates and results in state S' plus undo information.

nodes.title: Reachable-state supply bound
nodes.statement: For every reachable chain state, the UTXO total plus genesis subsidy is at most the issued subsidy at its next height.

assumptions.name: hR
assumptions.meaning: State S is reachable in the model.

nodes.title: UTXO maximum supply
nodes.statement: For every reachable state, the UTXO total is strictly below MAX_MONEY.

assumptions.name: hR
assumptions.meaning: State S is reachable in the model.

nodes.title: Reachability implies well-formedness
nodes.statement: Every state reachable in the formal chain model satisfies its WellFormed predicate.

assumptions.name: h
assumptions.meaning: The chain state S is reachable.

semantic.explanation: Subsidy issuance cap is a candidate input for the reachable-state supply argument; full proof-term use remains unverified.

Reachability-related structural conditions are candidates for the supply induction.
